questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road. Always increase your following distance when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do at a broken traffic signal?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
Go through if the intersection looks clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic signal like a four-way stop. Always come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: Let off the gas first and let the vehicle slow down. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed significantly.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. Be ready to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates raise.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates raise.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing with warning signs or gates. Driving around lowered gates is illegal.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Keep traffic away from work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones protect both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, vehicles, and workers in bright vests to guide you safely through.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, alcohol's effects will only go away by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Showers, coffee, and exercise do not speed this up. It takes about one hour per drink.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait for the vehicle to finish turning first.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Eating and drinking cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrup and cold medicine with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs impair driving: prescription sedatives, illegal drugs, and over-the-counter medicines like cough syrup and allergy pills.

questions.question: You can spot an aggressive driver by:

options.text: The number of passengers in the car.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for erratic and unsafe lane changes. If you see an aggressive driver, stay away from them. Do not challenge them.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let an aggressive driver pass and stay away from them. Do not compete with other drivers.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means greater impairment.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and pass them constantly, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination faster and safer.

questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each pass increases your chance of a collision.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area and take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine and energy drinks are not a real replacement for sleep.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Not watching for workers and equipment

questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic and keep more distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. All children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the right lane is ending. Be ready for cars merging into your lane.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street
Only if a crossing guard is present

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If both lines are solid, no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would behind a car
Follow farther behind than you would behind a car
Drive to the right side and wait to pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther behind than you would behind a car
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. Stay farther back to stay safe.

questions.question: How do alcohol and drugs affect driving?

options.text: They slow reaction time and reduce coordination

questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow the nervous system. They reduce alertness, slow your reaction time, and hurt your coordination.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane
questions.explanation: Stay calm during a blowout. Hold the wheel tightly and take your foot off the gas. Gently apply the brakes once the car slows down.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems
They create vibration and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they left the road

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and sound to alert drowsy drivers that they left the road
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn sleepy or inattentive drivers they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or light.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding above the limit or driving too fast for conditions
Getting enough rest and staying alert
Looking around and focusing on driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding above the limit or driving too fast for conditions
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many accidents. Drive at legal speeds and match the traffic flow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign marks a pedestrian crosswalk.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:
questions.explanation: When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes will soon combine into one lane.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or switch drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or switch drivers
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: Before driving while taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about side effects
Open your window and drive slowly

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about side effects
questions.explanation: Many medicines can affect driving ability. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine might affect your driving.
